mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in one month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive after controlling for lagged confidence indices (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates earnings expectations and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified growth period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -2% followed by a rebound above -1% suggests resolving supply bottlenecks, which typically precedes a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below -2% then crosses above -1% in the following month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain negative during the post-rebound period (rolling mean p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, it indicates a shift toward accommodative policy, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during the prior 3-month tightening phase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining payroll growth (PAYEMS < -2%) coupled with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggest a labor market cooling that dampens equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below -2% for two consecutive months and UNRATE increases by at least 0.1 percentage points
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative deviation during the cooling period (p > 0.05).
